edges.label: reaches_threshold
edges.reason: The assertion correctly identifies a fundamental neurophysiological principle: action potentials are triggered only when membrane voltage reaches a specific threshold potential. This general knowledge directly addresses the identified gap regarding the 'all-or-nothing' nature of action potentials versus graded signals, which is implied in the source text but not explicitly detailed. The relation 'reaches_threshold' accurately captures this necessary condition without contradicting the source context or inventing unsupported claims about the specific case.
edges.intended_fact: An action potential is triggered only when the membrane voltage reaches a specific threshold potential, distinguishing it from graded signals.
edges.link_reading: The link represents a necessary condition where an 'action potential' (event) triggers only upon the 'membrane voltage' (property) reaching a specific level, explicitly distinguishing this from graded signals.
edges.definition: The source event triggers only upon attaining a specific voltage level in the target.

provenance.text:
A typical neuron has a cell body, dendrites, and an axon. The cell body contains the nucleus, while dendrites receive many of the signals arriving from other neurons. The axon conducts action potentials toward its terminals, allowing the neuron to communicate with other cells.

An action potential involves a rapid change in the voltage across the neuron's membrane. Opening voltage-gated sodium channels allows sodium ions to enter the neuron during depolarization. The subsequent opening of voltage-gated potassium channels allows potassium ions to leave, contributing to repolarization. Myelin can increase the speed of action-potential conduction along an axon.

At a chemical synapse, an arriving action potential opens calcium channels in the presynaptic terminal. Calcium entry triggers the release of neurotransmitter from synaptic vesicles into the synaptic cleft. The neurotransmitter binds to receptors on the postsynaptic cell. Depending on the receptor, this binding can increase or decrease the likelihood of a postsynaptic action potential.
